value.rationale: This is a natural, two-parameter, infinite graph family, and the exact minimum over all edge-ℓ1 cut projections reveals a sharp symmetry-surviving nonorthogonality phenomenon. For every clique size \(m\ge3\) and independent size \(n\ge2\) there is a strict orthogonal cost, absent for \(m=2\). The gap tends to \(3/14\) along \(m=n\), so it is macroscopic, not a routine finite-instance correction. The distinction bears on optimal Banach complementability in graph incidence geometries.
